fictional_reviews.text: [Fictional review] Imagined lane-defense fan: the 5x9 solar economy with a per-lane emergency drone, shovel, pause and x2 speed feels like the classic formula with a fresh AI-parody skin, and the Bio-Laboratorio mind-control twist plus a 3-phase AGI finale with two endings gives the 24-level campaign a real arc.

[Fictional review] Made-up casual browser player: the ally-AI cards and four selectable companions sound like a fun second economy on top of the planting, but with zero gameplay screenshots or video I cannot judge readability, pacing, or whether 15 plants and 22 robots stay balanced across five zones.

[Fictional review] Invented procedural-art nerd take: 100% code-drawn emoji-face art, a soundtrack composed in GDScript, synthesized effects, zero third-party assets, everything data-driven in .tres files with headless script checks and self-playing autotest bots? Absurd craft for a free browser tower defense.

how_to_play: Open https://yefry08.github.io/plantas-vs-ia/ in a browser (no install; progress saves in the browser via IndexedDB).
Pick a level on the level-select screen and choose your seed lineup plus one of 4 allied-AI companions.
Pick a plant card on top (keys 1-6) and plant it on a grid cell of the 5-lane x 9-column lawn; collect falling sun for energy.
Tap falling suns and tokens; spend tokens on 6 allied-AI cards (e.g. tap card, then a robot) and tap your companion portrait when it glows for its active skill.
Use the shovel (S) to remove plants, right-click or Esc to cancel selection, and the II / x1 buttons (Esc/P, F) for pause and double speed.
Survive all waves without robots crossing your lawn; use the per-lane emergency drone as a last resort, and beat all 24 campaign levels across 5 zones plus the 3-phase La AGI boss.
mechanics: Lane tower defense on a 5-lane x 9-column grid: plants hold the lawn against waves of AI-parody robots marching per lane
Solar energy economy with falling suns, sun producers, and token currency powering 6 allied-AI cards
6 allied-AI cards: area self-destruct, single shutdown, lane-wide shutdown, alignment (convert robot), Red Team reveal/debuff, and Vaccine cure/protect
4 selectable allied-AI companions with passives and tap-to-activate abilities plus in-match commentary (danger lanes, idle energy, available cards)
24-level campaign across 5 zones including the Bio-Laboratorio where bio-weapon robots seize control of the player's plants
Final boss La AGI with 3 phases and 2 endings (including an alignment ending via 3 Alignment cards in phase 3) plus per-robot card resistances
Per-lane emergency drone, shovel, pause and x2 speed; fully playable with mouse or touch, keyboard optional
Fully data-driven balance in .tres files (plants, robots, cards, allies, levels) with headless script checks and self-playing autotest bots

rating.reason: Closest comparators: OSRS Tower Defense (52, fellow lane/map TD with 12 forgeable towers, 61 monsters, 130 waves and dense inspected gameplay frames), Kart Royale (50, complete 3D arcade loop with polished frames but thin systems), neverquest (45, deepest prior systems scope but text-UI only), and Taipo (35, fellow tower defense with one small map and three towers). Plantas vs IA clearly exceeds Taipo on authored depth (15 plants, 22 robots, 6 cards, 4 companions, 24 levels in 5 zones, 3-phase boss with 2 endings, autotest bots, verified live web build) and beats neverquest on real-time loop plus a complete playable export, but sits just below OSRS TD and Kart Royale because no gameplay screenshot or video could be inspected (repo tree holds zero image files; the only retrievable image is the default Godot engine splash), and there is no playthrough, performance, or balance verification — source and docs alone do not prove playability, performance, or balance. 0 stars/0 forks and a two-week-old repo reinforce prototype status despite strong scope.

reconstructed_prompt: Build Plantas vs IA: a lane tower-defense in Godot 4 (GDScript) for the browser, plants vs AI-parody robots. 5 lanes x 9 columns, solar energy plus token economy, 15 plants, 22 parody robots, 6 allied-AI cards, 4 selectable AI companions with passives and tap abilities, emergency drone per lane, shovel, pause and x2 speed. 24-level campaign across 5 zones including a Bio-Lab with mind-control enemies and a 3-phase final AGI boss with two endings. 100% procedural vector/emoji-face art, code-composed music and synthesized SFX, zero third-party assets, everything data-driven in .tres files, saves in user:// (IndexedDB on web), headless script checks plus self-playing autotest modes, Godot Web export (Compatibility renderer, no threads) hosted on GitHub Pages, mouse/touch first with optional keyboard shortcuts.

source_analysis.finding: Repository yefry08/plantas-vs-ia is public, not a fork, described as 'Tower defense por carriles en Godot 4: plantas contra robots IA. Jugable en el navegador.', primary language GDScript, homepage set to the playable Pages URL, 0 stars, 0 forks.
GitHub languages endpoint reports only GDScript (283302 bytes); no other language is used by the game.

README documents the full game: 5 lanes x 9 columns, solar energy, per-lane emergency drone, shovel, pause and x2 speed; 15 plants, 22 robots, 6 allied-AI cards, 4 AI companions; 24-level campaign in 5 zones plus final boss La AGI (3 phases, 2 endings); Bio-Laboratorio mind-control zone; 100% procedural art, code-composed music, synthesized SFX, zero third-party assets, data-driven .tres content, saves in user:// (IndexedDB on web).

README control table shows mouse/touch columns and optional keyboard (1-6 plant cards, Q/W AI cards, S shovel, Esc cancel, Esc/P pause, F speed), and states the game can be played start to finish with mouse alone or touch on mobile.
project.godot sets emulate_mouse_from_touch=true, 1280x720 viewport, canvas_items/keep stretch, GL Compatibility renderer, main scene main_menu.tscn, and SaveManager/GameState/AudioManager autoloads.
export_presets.cfg defines a Web preset (thread_support=false, export path build/web/index.html), matching the documented no-COOP/COEP GitHub Pages and itch.io publishing flow.

Repo file tree holds 247 files with zero image files; scenes (main_menu, level_select, seed_select, level, credits), scripts (autoload, data, components, game, plants, robots, ui, art), 24 level files level_01-level_24.tres, plant/robot/card/ally .tres data, tools/generate_content.gd and tools/generate_music.gd, and audio/*.wav files.
Sample level_01.tres is a LevelData resource with WaveData sub-resources (durations, robot groups, counts, intervals, lanes), confirming the documented data-driven wave design.

Playable URL returns HTTP 200 and serves a Godot web export shell (canvas, index.js, index.wasm ~39.5MB, index.pck ~3.1MB, GODOT_CONFIG with threads disabled), i.e. the playable game rather than a repo or promo page.

The only retrievable image at the playable site is index.png, inspected at 800x600: the default Godot engine logo (blue robot head + 'GODOT Game engine' on black) — engine branding, not gameplay output — so no gameplay screenshot could be inspected or scored.

Play is solo lane defense against AI robot waves with browser-local saves; no human multiplayer mode is documented anywhere, so human-player count is 1 and mode is single-player (AI robots and the allied-AI helper are not human players).

No AI creation-model attribution was found in the inspected README or project config; AI parody robots are in-fiction content, not documented tooling used to build the game, so creation_models is empty.

No catalog entry matches this game: no existing games/ directory or README references this repository, playable URL, or project (searched for yefry08/plantas variants); the fellow tower-defense entries (OSRS Tower Defense, Taipo) are different projects by different authors, so catalog_slug is null.
